run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T07:57:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: RequestErrorRate fired for frontend because frontend began returning HTTP 500 on /api/data and /api/checkout immediately after the ad and payment Deployments were rollout-restarted at 2026-11-16T07:56:15Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt). The replacement pods were reported Ready 2-3 s after container start, but no readiness probe exists on any otel-demo workload, so traffic was routed to pods whose gRPC servers were not yet listening: ad logged 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' only at 08:02:36Z and payment logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 07:57:28Z. Both new containers were heavily CPU-throttled during startup (ad CFS throttled-period ratio 0.92-0.94 from 07:58 to 08:03 versus ~0.26 on frontend; payment 0.97 at 07:58). Frontend client spans record gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE connect ECONNREFUSED to the ad Service ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080 and checkout's Charge client spans record the same to the payment Service ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080. Frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were exactly zero in the 30 minutes before the restart, peaked at 2.5777777777777775/s at 08:01:49Z (identical to the alert's reported value) and were zero again in the 2-minute window ending 08:05:49Z. The ad Deployment is the dominant origin (~387 GET /api/data error spans vs ~43 /api/checkout error spans); the payment Deployment is a second, smaller contributor with the same mechanism. Nodes were healthy and the demo services reached during the sampled traces (cart, currency, product-catalog, quote, shipping) returned no errors.

claims.text: Frontend span error rate: in the 2-minute rate series of traces_span_metrics_calls_total by status_code for service_name=frontend, STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0 at every evaluation from 07:34:49Z through 07:55:49Z, became non-zero at 07:57:49Z (1.0111/s), peaked at 2.5777777777777775/s at 08:01:49Z, was 1.6889/s at 08:03:49Z and 0 at 08:05:49Z and 08:07:49Z, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET stayed roughly 29-37/s throughout.

No frontend error spans remained in the last 10 minutes of the window: every frontend span_name with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR (GET, grpc.oteldemo.*, executing api route (pages) /api/data, /api/checkout, tcp.connect, etc.) had increase = 0 over the 10 minutes ending 08:13:54Z.

Affected - frontend's own error spans over the 35 minutes ending 08:13:54Z: GET /api/data 386.64, GET 386.64, executing api route (pages) /api/data 386.64 and client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 386.64; POST /api/checkout 42.62, POST 42.62, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 42.62 and client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 42.62; frontend tcp.connect 15.22. (Span counts, not unique request counts.)

Affected - frontend-proxy and checkout show their own error spans for the same requests over the 35 minutes ending 08:13:54Z: frontend-proxy ingress 451.59 and router frontend egress 429.26 STATUS_CODE_ERROR; checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 34.83 and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 34.83 STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

Exact transport errors in the sampled erroneous traces (07:57:21-07:57:23Z): frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carries rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080'; checkout client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge carries rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with 'dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused'; the enclosing frontend spans (GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout) have http.status_code 500 and otel.status_code ERROR.

The refused addresses are the Service ClusterIPs: Service ad has clusterIP 100.65.180.246 with port 8080->8080 selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, and Service payment has clusterIP 100.70.188.60 with port 8080->8080 selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment.

Both Deployments were rollout-restarted at 07:56:15Z: the ad and payment pod templates carry annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T07:56:15Z and deployment revision 2, with deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2 ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 created at 07:56:15Z while revision-1 ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 are at 0 desired replicas.

The rollout events at 07:56:15-07:56:19Z are a normal controller replacement, not damage: ad SuccessfulCreate ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and ScalingReplicaSet ad 0->1, ad-554b849958 1->0 and SuccessfulDelete of ad-554b849958-mbnxm (Killing 'Stopping container ad'); the same pattern for payment (payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 created/started, payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb deleted).

The replacement pods were Ready almost immediately and never restarted: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 container started 07:56:17Z, Ready/ContainersReady True at 07:56:18Z, restartCount 0, lastState empty; payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 container started 07:56:18Z, Ready True at 07:56:19Z, restartCount 0, lastState empty; both run on node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884.

No readiness or liveness probe is defined on the ad or payment containers (nor on any otel-demo Deployment container except otel-collector, which has both); ad's CPU limit is 50m and payment's is 20m.

The new ad container did not bind its port for minutes: its only startup logs are 'Ad service starting.' at 08:00:42.827Z and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 08:02:36.226Z, and the first request log lines ('no baggage found in context', 'Targeted ad request received...') begin at 08:03:22Z.
The new payment container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 07:57:28.223Z and its first 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs at 07:58:03.292Z.

The new ad and payment pods were CPU-throttled far above the frontend baseline: container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total/container_cpu_cfs_periods_total was 0.92 at 07:58:00Z and 0.87-0.94 through 08:04:00Z for ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6, 0.97 at 07:58:00Z for payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 (falling to ~0.68 at 08:00:00Z), versus 0.26-0.34 for the long-running frontend pod over the same period.

The ad service stopped serving after the restart and resumed later: ad server spans oteldemo.AdService/GetAds were a steady ~50-90 per 2-minute window until 07:57:49Z, then 0 in every 2-minute window from 07:58:49Z through 08:04:49Z, and 96 in the window ending 08:06:49Z.

Baseline before the restart shows no frontend errors at all: over the 30 minutes ending 07:56:00Z every frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR series (GET, GET /api/data, POST /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, executing api route..., tcp.connect) had increase = 0, so the error burst began with the 07:56:15Z rollout.

Chronic flagd EventStream error spans are background noise and were already present before the incident: over the 30 minutes ending 07:56:00Z ad flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream had 1.04 error spans, recommendation 3.10 and fraud-detection 1.04; after the incident ad's only error span series is the same EventStream (1.01 over 35 minutes ending 08:13:54Z) with ResolveBoolean at 0, so nothing indicates an ad application-level failure.

Node-level resource pressure is not supported: all 5 nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False (including i-0e9f8b08cc290a884 where the new ad and payment pods run).

Checked and healthy - the payment application itself did not fail once reachable: payment service's own error span series (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect) are all 0 over the 35 minutes ending 08:13:54Z, while the failures are transport-level on checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge.

Checked and healthy - cart, currency, product-catalog, quote and shipping returned no errors on the paths exercised by the failing traces: their spans in the sampled erroneous traces (cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and HGET, currency Currency/Convert otel.status_code OK, product-catalog GetProduct, quote POST /getquote, shipping /get-quote) all show error_rows 0.

Container crash, OOMKill or crash-loop on ad/payment is rejected: both replacement containers have restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and the only events in the namespace are the graceful rollout events (Killing, SuccessfulDelete, SuccessfulCreate, ScalingReplicaSet, Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started) with no OOMKilled, BackOff or Unhealthy events.

Image-pull or scheduling failure is rejected: the events for both new pods record 'Container image "ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad" already present on machine' (and the payment equivalent), followed by Created and Started container, on node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884.

Causal mechanism: the 07:56:15Z rollout restart of the ad and payment Deployments replaced the only endpoints of both Services; because the containers define no readiness probe, the new pods were published as Ready 2-3 s after start while their gRPC servers were still starting, so connects to the ad ClusterIP (100.65.180.246:8080) and payment ClusterIP (100.70.188.60:8080) were refused until the servers bound their ports, surfacing as frontend HTTP 500 on GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout and raising RequestErrorRate.

The multi-minute delay before ad listened is plausibly caused by CPU starvation at its 50m limit: the ad container was CFS-throttled in 0.92-0.94 of periods from 07:58 to 08:03 (payment 0.97 at 07:58) and only logged 'Ad service starting.' 3.4 minutes after container start and bound port 8080 6.3 minutes after container start; no throttling or runtime metric is available to prove the internal start-up path.

RequestErrorRate is most likely computed from the frontend span error rate even though the expression could not be read: the alert's 'current: 2.5777777777777775' is numerically identical to the 2-minute per-second increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} at 08:01:49Z, and the error rate was above 0 only from 07:57:49Z to 08:03:49Z, matching the alert start 07:57:49Z.

Add a readinessProbe (gRPC health or TCP 8080) to the ad and payment containers so Service endpoints are only published after the server is listening, and do not rely on container start as readiness; today no otel-demo Deployment except otel-collector defines one.
Raise the ad (50m) and payment (20m) CPU limits/requests and re-test start-up time; both replacement pods were throttled in >90% of CFS periods at start and ad needed ~6 minutes to bind 8080.

Avoid simultaneous single-replica rollout restarts of ad and payment (e.g. stagger them or keep a surge pod ready) and confirm with change management who issued kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T07:56:15Z, since change history is not available in this run.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for all alert rules in this Prometheus, so the alert's exact expression, window and thresholds are unverified; the metric linkage rests only on the exact numeric match of 2.5777777777777775.

change_history is not an integrated data source in this run, so who or what triggered the ad and payment rollout restarts at 2026-11-16T07:56:15Z (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) cannot be verified.

Jaeger held traces only up to about 2026-11-16T07:57:24Z (source_end_at of the trace queries), so error traces after that time could not be sampled; the later error timing (07:58-08:05) rests on Prometheus span metrics only.

Logs of the terminated pre-rollout pods (ad-554b849958-mbnxm, payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb) and the previous container instances are not retrievable, so their shutdown behaviour and the exact moment their endpoints were removed are unknown.
Endpoint/EndpointSlice history is unavailable (only current cluster state can be read), so the exact interval during which ad/payment Services had no accepting backend cannot be directly observed.

The cause of the earlier flagd ReplicaSet replacement (flagd-56d9c6c679 created 2026-11-16T07:24:12Z, replacing flagd-c47676d99) is unexplained; it predates the error onset and no error evidence ties it to this alert, but change history for it is missing.

Ad container internals between 07:56:17Z and 08:00:42Z produced no stdout lines, so what the process was doing before 'Ad service starting.' is inferred from CPU throttling only, not directly observed.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Prometheus/Alertmanager instance that owns it to confirm the metric, window and the threshold that produced 2.5777777777777775.
Review with the platform/change owner the two rollout restarts issued at 2026-11-16T07:56:15Z on Deployments ad and payment.

After adding readinessProbes and larger CPU limits, repeat a rolling restart of ad and payment and confirm that no ECONNREFUSED spans to the ad/payment ClusterIPs appear and that frontend GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout stay at HTTP 200.
Consider pre-warming/JVM start-up tuning for the ad service to reduce the ~6 minute period before it binds port 8080 under a 50m CPU limit.
